rationale: The frozen candidate source_sha256 is 3e91364af58e820c71cb4bc2ae461aabab73eb3792442770ed1be7460066731c, while all author/independent-agent reports bind their evidence to 8e962bf56e385381cd03d9c0e77057655314e5634c628130e4d8aa8988258288. This source identity drift prevents attributing the reviewed evidence to the frozen source.

The four concrete draft test files hash to the candidate manifest's test_sha256 values, but their contents are not the same as the separate test_source/entrypoint_test_source/ddp_test_source strings in the author reports. The evidence therefore has multiple test variants and is not a single frozen, independently executed test set.

The recorded independent runtime artifacts contain agent-produced test-source strings, not execution results demonstrating that these concrete files ran against the frozen trainer. No verified pass/fail output for all four reviewed concrete tests is present in the inspected artifacts.

The concrete tests do provide non-self-referential reference values, call a real two-rank DDP model path, and call trainer.main with a synthetic fixture; these strengths do not resolve the source/test identity and execution-evidence gaps.
